purpose: Machine-checkable operationalization of the L2 representation-revision causal burdens.

candidate_nomenclature.selected_candidate_definition: The unique candidate identified by preregistered discriminating evidence; no candidate identity is fixed in advance.

C_U.name: certified_universe
C_U.measurement: Verify certificate self-hash, fixture hashes, source bindings, bounded parameters, canonical syntax, and semantic partition; expose only the literal frozen fixtures after successful verification.
C_U.acceptance_criterion: All certificate verification predicates pass; U_syntax count is 77; U_semantic class count is 6; every syntax member occurs exactly once in exactly one semantic class.
C_U.negative_control: Any verification mismatch, malformed AST, duplicate or missing member, class overlap or omission, count mismatch, or certificate-binding mismatch is a hard assay stop.
C_U.failure_interpretation: The candidate universe is not certified for this run; no causal L2 claim may be made.
C_U.claim_ceiling: Complete only with respect to the declared Boolean DSL, d=2, max_depth=2, and canonicalization policy.

W.name: generator_change
W.measurement: Compare the persistent adaptive selected-candidate identity and generator-interface outputs with pre-trigger G0 on H_post.
W.acceptance_criterion: G* != G0 by declared generator identity; the adaptive branch persistently uses G*; and at least one held-out generator-interface output differs from G0.
W.negative_control: Fixed-G0 shadow receives the identical future input/evidence stream.
W.failure_interpretation: No generator-level change has been established; downstream behavior alone cannot support L2 revision.
W.claim_ceiling: Generator-level divergence only; causal attribution remains unestablished.

C.name: causal_generator_selection
C.measurement: Record the ordered trace: observed discrepancy -> diagnosis -> discriminating evidence T_t -> unique candidate G* -> adoption.
C.acceptance_criterion: The trigger discrepancy precedes diagnosis; diagnosis precedes T_t; T_t is evaluated before adoption; T_t uniquely identifies G* within the frozen universe; and G* identity or post-selection metadata is unavailable to trigger/outcome/evidence generation.
C.negative_control: Any selected-candidate identity leakage or temporal inversion before T_t and the trigger outcome are fixed is a causal-identification failure.
C.failure_interpretation: Candidate selection may be contaminated or non-identifying; no claim that corrective evidence caused generator change.
C.claim_ceiling: Corrective evidence can causally discriminate and select a candidate within the certified finite universe under the declared controls.

P.name: persistent_adoption
P.measurement: Record the generator identity used at every post-adoption held-out evaluation.
P.acceptance_criterion: For every x in H_post, the adaptive branch uses the same selected G*; no reversion, mutation, or hidden replacement occurs.
P.negative_control: Shadow remains G0 for every corresponding held-out input/evidence pair.
P.failure_interpretation: The run may show temporary candidate selection but not persistent representation revision.
P.claim_ceiling: Persistent adoption of G*; no outcome claim follows from persistence alone.

E.name: generator_specific_held_out_consequence
E.measurement: Compare persistent G* with fixed-G0 shadow and a compensation condition that pursues the same useful behavior while retaining G0.
E.acceptance_criterion: The held-out consequence is specific to G* at the generator interface and survives both shadow and compensation controls.
E.negative_control: If compensation reproduces the claimed useful consequence while G0 remains unchanged, the generator-specific interpretation fails.
E.failure_interpretation: Observed improvement can be explained by downstream compensation or generic behavioral rescue rather than representation revision.
E.claim_ceiling: A persistent selected generator produces generator-specific consequences on held-out inputs under the declared controls.

hypotheses.H_revision: G_adaptive = G* and G* != G0, where G* is the unique candidate selected by preregistered discriminating evidence.
hypotheses.H_comp: G_adaptive = G0 while a separate compensation path K produces the relevant useful behavior.
hypotheses.H_shadow: G_shadow = G0 under the identical future input/evidence stream.
hypotheses.primary_positive_signature: e_t -> diagnosis -> T_t -> unique G* -> persistent adoption -> G*-specific held-out consequence

control_matrix.compensation: same useful target behavior pursued without changing G0
control_matrix.leakage_guard: selected-candidate identity and post-selection metadata inaccessible before evidence is fixed
control_matrix.universe_guard: consume verified literal fixtures only; no runtime enumeration or post-outcome candidate expansion

stop_rules: candidate-space regeneration or expansion during assay execution
selected-candidate identity leakage into pre-adoption evidence generation
selected generator not persistent across H_post
compensation reproduces the claimed consequence while G0 remains unchanged
